item.title: Chinese Peacekeepers Complete 1st Long-range Cross-sector Joint Patrol In South Sudan
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
By Wang Shuai, Yang Shiwei and Wu Zhongwei JUBA, Sept. 8 -- The 12th Chinese Peacekeeping Infantry Battalion to South Sudan (Juba), together with UN military observers and UN police, successfully completed a long-range cross-sector joint patrol recently. Passing through areas such as Yei and Morobo, the long patrol lasted five days and four nights and covered more than 400 kilometers, passing through several remote areas of South Sudan. Along the way, the Chinese peacekeepers passed through 52 checkpoints and 12 areas without signal coverage and traversed two conflict-sensitive zones. During the mission, the Chinese peacekeepers held multiple discussions to assess the security situation and the local living conditions in the mission area, and carried out humanitarian assistance activities such as donating supplies. This mission comprehensively tested the peacekeeping troops' combat-oriented capabilities in long-distance maneuvering, contingency response, and comprehensive support. (Cameramen: He Yuxin and Tang Han)

item.title: China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint exercise kicks off in Vientiane
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
By Zhou Na, Liu Xiaowei, Chi Xuedong, Zhang Tianyu, Yang Chao, Yin Chuandong, Tan Yuzhou and Wang Yong VIENTIANE, Sept. 8 -- The China-Laos "Peace Train-2026" joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise and medical service activities kicked off in Vientiane, the capital of Laos, on September 7, 2026. Since 2017, the Chinese and Lao militaries have held six consecutive China-Laos "Peace Train" joint exercises. This series of exercise has become a platform for enhancing the two militaries' capabilities in joint rescue and response to natural disasters. Set against the backdrop of international humanitarian medical rescue following a super typhoon disaster, the exercise features a three-tier command structure and a four-tier rescue system. Using medical trains, field medical treatment equipment and unmanned intelligent equipment, the two sides will organize mixed joint training, full-process joint rehearsals and live-force exercises. The exercise aims to explore operational models for cross-border joint medical rescue and further enhance the medical support coordination and emergency response capabilities of the two militaries. The exercise will run until late September, with more than 700 personnel from both sides participating. During this period, medical services, cultural exchanges, and other activities will also be organized.

item.title: Xi holds phone talks with British PM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday held phone talks with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Congratulating Burnham on assuming office as British prime minister, Xi said that China and Britain are comprehensive strategic partners. Despite differences in their social systems and national conditions, the two countries share more common interests than differences. Xi urged the two sides to respect and trust each other, overcome differences, seek common ground and expand mutually beneficial cooperation. Both governments are committed to developing their economies and improving people's well-being, and the two countries can complement each other's strengths and facilitate each other's development, Xi said. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China will further expand opening up in such areas as education, healthcare and finance, all of which offer great potential for bilateral cooperation, Xi said. Pointing out that China and Britain are both major countries in science and technology with rich resources in education, culture, sports and other fields, Xi called on the two sides to adopt an open and forward-looking approach and strengthen exchanges and cooperation in various fields. Xi expressed the hope that the British side will fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese investors. Xi noted that China and Britain, as permanent members of the UN Security Council and major economies in the world, both support multilateralism and open trade and uphold the central role of the United Nations. The two sides should strengthen communication and coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, the Group of 20 and the World Trade Organization, and promote an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Burnham agreed, saying that he had served as mayor of Manchester for many years and maintained friendly exchanges with China for years. President Xi's visit to Manchester during his state visit to Britain in 2015 had a significant impact on promoting local exchanges and cooperation with China, Burnham said. Burnham said Britain is willing to maintain continuity in its policy toward China and remain firmly committed to developing a long-term, stable strategic partnership between Britain and China. Britain is ready to conduct high-level exchanges with China, advance bilateral cooperation in various fields, strengthen people-to-people exchanges, and restore bilateral relations to their historic high, so as to better benefit the peoples of both countries, Burnham added. Burnham said that Britain's position on the Taiwan question remains unchanged. Amid the current turbulent and complex international landscape undergoing changes, Britain and China, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, should promote the resolution of international hotspot issues through dialogue, jointly address global challenges such as climate change, and work together to safeguard world stability and prosperity, Burnham added. Burnham spoke highly of China's efficient and effective response to the mudslide disaster that struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, and expressed appreciation for China's assistance to affected British citizens.

item.title: Asian coast guard high-level meeting to address non-traditional security challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
By Li Lei The upcoming 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies (HACGAM) High-Level Meeting will focus on non-traditional security challenges and ways to manage risks and crises amid a "complex and volatile" regional maritime security situation, a China Coast Guard spokesman said on Monday. The annual forum, set to open Tuesday in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, will also explore effective ways to promote cross-border cooperation and safeguard maritime peace and stability, spokesman Liu Dejun said. Liu noted that the meeting has evolved over more than two decades, expanding its membership to include countries and regions across East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia, and even some outside the region. Its institutional framework has grown increasingly robust, while cooperation has broadened into new areas. The organizing of HACGAM meetings follows China's chairing of the North Pacific Coast Guard Forum last year — an expansion from a six-nation "North Pacific Plus" event to a broader pan-Asia-Pacific forum. Liu said China remains committed to promoting its vision of a "maritime community with a shared future" and its Global Security Initiative, aiming to build consensus on regional maritime security governance. China hosted the HACGAM working-level meeting in May in Quanzhou, Fujian province, which provided technical support and outcomes that facilitated the opening of this week's high-level session.

item.title: China-Laos Peace Train 2026 Joint Humanitarian Medical Rescue Exercise to Be Held in Laos
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
BEIJING, Sept. 4 -- China-Laos Peace Train 2026 joint humanitarian medical rescue exercise will be held in Laos in September, said Senior Colonel Jiang Bin, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, on Friday. Taking international humanitarian medical rescue in a super typhoon disaster as its theme, the exercise focuses on such training subjects as joint on-site search and rescue, casualty evacuation, health and epidemic prevention, and psychological rescue. During the event, the Chinese side will also provide medical services for Lao military personnel and civilians. As the sixth exercise of this series, the joint exercise will further deepen and expand pragmatic exchange and cooperation in such fields as disaster medical rescue, tropical disease control and prevention, and infectious disease prevention and control, enhance the two militaries' capabilities in joint medical-service command, joint rescue, and joint prevention and control, and better provide quality public security goods for regional countries and peoples.
